title: What is a Neural Network?
description: How interconnected neurons, layers, weights, and activation functions turn raw data into predictions, and which network architectures are built on this idea.
content:
**Neural network** is a model inspired by the human brain that consists of interconnected units (neurons) working together to process information.

A neural network is organized into layers:
• Input layer - receives raw data
• Hidden layer - one or more layers that perform feature extraction and transformation
• Output layer - produces the final prediction

Every neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs, adds a bias, and passes the result through an activation function to introduce non-linearity.

Every connection between neurons has a **weight** that indicates its importance. During training, algorithms like **backpropagation** adjust these weights to minimize the difference between the network's predictions and the actual targets.

Activation functions introduce non-linearity into the network, which is crucial: without it, the network would simply represent a linear transformation of its inputs. Common activation functions include:
• Sigmoid - maps input to the range (0, 1), making it suitable for binary classification, however it suffers from vanishing gradients
• Hyperbolic Tangent (tanh) - outputs values between -1 and 1, typically providing faster convergence than sigmoid since its output is zero-centered
• ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) - returns the output directly if positive, otherwise it outputs zero; computationally effective and alleviates the vanishing gradient problem
• Leaky ReLU - a variant of ReLU that allows a small, non-zero gradient when the input is negative, helping to prevent the dead neuron problem (when weights are updated in such a way that a neuron always outputs zero and does not contribute to the learning process)
• Softmax - converts a vector of raw scores (logits) into probabilities that sum to one, useful, for example, in multi-class classification

Among the neural network architectures there are:
• Feedforward neural networks
• Recurrent neural networks (RNN)
• Convolutional neural networks (CNN)
• Graph neural networks (GNN)
• Generative adversarial networks (GAN)
• Diffusion neural networks
• Autoencoder networks
• Transformer networks
